subject: MSA + Order Form: jurisdictional fallback and escrow access proposal
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pegasuspayments.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jaya Rao <jaya.rao@pegasuspayments.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pegasus proposed MSA redlines (jurisdiction + emergency access)

Sean —

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Legal ran the MSA redlines over the weekend and we attached a clean copy with comments (Pegasus_MSARedlines_v3.pdf). Two items they asked us to get clarity on for the signature-ready order form:

1) Governing law & forum: Pegasus prefers New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in New York state or federal courts for disputes.
2) Emergency/access carveouts: because Pegasus will hold transaction data and will need to enforce consumer protection claims quickly, they want an escrow / emergency access mechanism that allows temporary access to logs or a narrow set of metrics on an urgent basis under court order or escrow trustee direction.

They also flagged the arbitration clause: they are open to arbitration for most commercial disputes but want an explicit exception that permits them to seek preliminary injunctive relief in court (weaker carveouts are fine).

Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can accept NY governing law, and what Redwood’s preferred language is for a "break-glass" emergency preservation path? We want to be sure sign-off timelines don't slip.

Best,
Tom
Head of Legal Operations
Pegasus Payments

Attachments: Pegasus_MSARedlines_v3.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pegasuspayments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus proposed MSA redlines (jurisdiction + emergency access)

Tom —

Appreciate the clear note and the marked-up PDF. Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (sales ops). Quick answers up front:

- Governing law: Redwood historically prefers California law for Masters but we can be flexible. For enterprise deals with sensitive payment flows we can move to New York law if paired with a one-way enforcement carve for Redwood (reason: predictability for our infra controls).
- Emergency access/escrow: Redwood supports a narrow emergency preservation path but has concerns about open-ended escrow access to logs. We propose a documented "break-glass" process that:
  * requires written notice to Redwood and a 24-hour (or judicially shorter) opportunity to respond,
  * limits the scope to specific logs/indicators required to address the immediate consumer protection/chargeback event, and
  * requires any escrow trustee access to be subject to a narrowly scoped court order or joint-appointment trustee process.

Laura/Karthik — can you review Pegasus’s redlines and propose language that preserves Redwood’s ability to protect customer data while giving Pegasus practical emergency recourse? If we can get language acceptable to both parties, I’ll prioritize executive review.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pegasuspayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus proposed MSA redlines (jurisdiction + emergency access)

Tom/Team —

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed Pegasus_MSARedlines_v3 and drafted a compromise that I think addresses both sides' concerns. Major points:

1) Governing law / forum
  * Proposed: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts of law principles. The parties agree that the courts located in the State of New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any proceeding seeking non‑monetary injunctive relief; provided, however, that either party may seek injunctive or other provisional relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo or protect confidential information or trade secrets pending resolution by arbitration or litigation."
  * Rationale: preserves Redwood's ability to seek narrow, urgent relief outside arbitration while agreeing to NY governing law and forum for court actions.

2) Arbitration / dispute resolution
  * Proposed: binding arbitration for commercial disputes administered by the American Arbitration Association (or another agreed provider) in New York; discovery/disclosure limits specifically carved for disputes involving security, data protection, or IP claims.

3) Emergency preservation / escrow access (break-glass)
  * Proposed a three-step protocol: (i) good-faith notice to Redwood, (ii) 8‑hour response window where Redwood can either provide the requested artifact under a limited protective order or consent to trustee access, (iii) if Redwood contests and no agreement is reached, Pegasus may apply for expedited judicial relief identifying the precise materials sought.
  * Trustee / escrow: recommend language that requires any trustee to be neutral and appointed by the parties jointly or by the court; any trustee access must be narrowly tailored and limited to the minimum necessary materials.

I attached a marked OrderForm clause (OrderForm_Pegasus_v2_marked.docx) and a short summary spreadsheet with proposed redlines (Redlines_Summary_Sean.xlsx).

Tom — happy to hop on a 20‑minute call to walk through the compromise language if that helps accelerate signoff.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pegasuspayments.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jaya Rao <jaya.rao@pegasuspayments.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus proposed MSA redlines (jurisdiction + emergency access)

Laura —

Thanks, this is helpful and a lot closer than our starting point. A few notes from Pegasus legal:

- The 8-hour response window is aggressive but acceptable provided there is a clear escalation path (we can accept 8 hours business-hours or 24 hours otherwise).
- Trustee appointment: Pegasus would like an independent escrow agent with experience handling payment systems; joint appointment is fine as long as we have an initial list of approved trustees.
- For injunctive carveout: PEG wants explicit confirmation that arbitration will not bar an emergency court filing to obtain temporary relief — your language above appears to allow that, which works.

We have two requests before we circulate to execs: (1) add a short procedural section describing who on each side gets the initial notice (name/role/email) for break-glass events, and (2) include a bullet confirming Redwood will not unilaterally purge the requested artifacts for 14 calendar days after notice.

If you can feed that in, we can move to commercial signoff on our side.

Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pegasuspayments.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pegasus proposed MSA redlines (jurisdiction + emergency access)

Tom/Laura —

Thanks — I've incorporated the two asks into the draft:

• Contact points: initial notice to be sent to "legal-incident@pegasuspayments.com" (or the named on-call person) and to Redwood's incident inbox "security-incident@redwoodinference.com" plus the contract signatory.
• Data preservation: Redwood will preserve requested artifacts and will not purge related logs for 14 calendar days following notice; Redwood will provide a short confirmation (timestamped) when preservation is in effect.

I've uploaded the updated OrderForm (OrderForm_Pegasus_v2_marked.docx) with inline edits and put a note in HubSpot. If you confirm the trustee candidate list and we have agreement on the 14-day hold, I'll route to finance for final pricing alignment and exec signatures.

Next steps: 20‑minute call Friday if needed; otherwise propose DocuSign circulation once both legal teams confirm.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
